accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the services provided by One Stop Centres (Sakhi)?
o: Medical, legal, counselling and shelter services under one roof
Only emergency police assistance and prosecution
Vocational training and permanent employment exclusively
Only temporary shelter and financial assistance
accepted.x: One Stop Centres, also known as Sakhi centres, provide medical, legal, counselling and shelter services under one roof to women affected by violence.
accepted.tq: Identify the option that combines the complete service package rather than a single function.
accepted.sec: Legal aid and support institutions - One Stop Centres, Women Helpline, fast track courts

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding legal aid and support institutions in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Women Helpline 181 provides emergency help and counselling.
2. ERSS 112 is a single emergency number supported through the Nirbhaya Fund.
3. Women Help Desks function in police stations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Women Helpline 181 provides emergency help and counselling, ERSS 112 is the single emergency number, and Women Help Desks operate in police stations.
accepted.tq: Check each institution against its specific function before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: Legal aid and support institutions - One Stop Centres, Women Helpline, fast track courts

accepted.s: As per the Andhra Pradesh figures cited for the relevant period, which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: One Stop Centres — 3 lakh plus calls
accepted.x: The cited Andhra Pradesh figures record 3,590 women helped through One Stop Centres and more than three lakh calls to Women Helpline 181.
accepted.tq: Match each numerical figure with the institution to which it specifically relates.
accepted.sec: Legal aid and support institutions - One Stop Centres, Women Helpline, fast track courts

accepted.s:
With reference to Fast Track Special Courts, consider the following statements:
1. There were 743 functional courts.
2. Of these, 394 were exclusive POCSO courts.
3. They had disposed of 3,39,644 cases as on 31 July 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: 743 Fast Track Special Courts were functional, including 394 exclusive POCSO courts, and 3,39,644 cases had been disposed of by 31 July 2025.
accepted.tq: Treat the court total, the exclusive POCSO subset and the disposal figure as separate numerical facts.
accepted.sec: Legal aid and support institutions - One Stop Centres, Women Helpline, fast track courts

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with Shakti Sadans in Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh figures mention 26 Shakti Sadans sheltering 950 trafficked women.
accepted.tq: Use the institution-specific numerical pair and reject figures belonging to other support mechanisms.
accepted.sec: Legal aid and support institutions - One Stop Centres, Women Helpline, fast track courts

accepted.s: Free legal aid for women and other eligible persons is provided through which institutional mechanism?
accepted.x: Free legal aid is provided through the Legal Services Authorities. Courts and police desks may support access to justice but are not the institution identified for providing free legal aid.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the institution providing legal aid from institutions providing emergency, police or judicial support.
accepted.sec: Legal aid and support institutions - One Stop Centres, Women Helpline, fast track courts

accepted.s: According to UNODC trafficking findings, which one of the following countries is identified as both a high origin country and a high destination country?
accepted.x: Bangladesh, India, Nepal and Pakistan are identified as high origin countries, while India and Pakistan are also identified as high destination countries.
accepted.tq: Separate the overlapping origin-and-destination category from countries listed only as origins.
accepted.sec: Trafficking - UNODC GLOTIP findings, US TIP tiers, forms

accepted.s: The GLOTIP 2016 finding that traffickers and victims often share the same national or ethnic background relates to which aspect of trafficking?
o: The compulsory involvement of only foreign nationals
The classification of countries into US TIP tiers
The social and demographic relationship between traffickers and victims
The exclusive role of state agencies in trafficking
accepted.x: GLOTIP 2016 highlighted that traffickers and victims often come from the same national or ethnic background. This is a finding about the relationship between perpetrators and victims, not about TIP classification.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise subject of the finding instead of confusing it with country ranking or tier classification.
accepted.sec: Trafficking - UNODC GLOTIP findings, US TIP tiers, forms

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the US Trafficking in Persons Report tiers:

List-I
 a. Tier 1
 b. Tier 2
 c. Tier 2 Watch List
 d. Tier 3

List-II
 i. Does not fully meet minimum standards but is making significant efforts
 ii. Not making significant efforts
 iii. Fully meets the minimum standards
 iv. Special watch-list category associated with Tier 2

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
accepted.x: Tier 1 fully meets the minimum standards; Tier 2 does not fully meet them but is making significant efforts; Tier 2 Watch List is the watch-list category; and Tier 3 represents countries not making significant efforts.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure pair Tier 1–fully meets standards and eliminate codes that disturb it.
accepted.sec: Trafficking - UNODC GLOTIP findings, US TIP tiers, forms

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the forms of trafficking covered by the CLA 2013 definition?
accepted.x: The listed forms include sex trafficking, forced or bonded labour, child trafficking, slavery and servitude, and organ removal. Voluntary migration without exploitation is not one of these forms.
accepted.tq: Find the option that falls outside the stated list and does not involve exploitation.
accepted.sec: Trafficking - UNODC GLOTIP findings, US TIP tiers, forms

accepted.s: The CLA 2013 definition covers the listed forms of trafficking irrespective of which factor?
accepted.x: The CLA 2013 definition covers the specified forms of trafficking irrespective of consent.
accepted.tq: Focus on the qualifying phrase that applies across all listed forms.
accepted.sec: Trafficking - UNODC GLOTIP findings, US TIP tiers, forms

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding India’s international obligations is correct?
o: India has ratified only the US Trafficking in Persons Report.
India has rejected all protocols concerning transnational organised crime.
India has ratified the UN Convention against Transnational Organized Crime and its protocols.
India has ratified only conventions relating to domestic labour and not transnational crime.
accepted.x: India has ratified the UN Convention against Transnational Organized Crime and its protocols.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a binding international convention and its protocols from an assessment report or domestic law.
accepted.sec: Trafficking - UNODC GLOTIP findings, US TIP tiers, forms

accepted.s: The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 was originally known as the:
o: Protection of Women from Traffic Act
accepted.x: The law originally started as the Suppression of Immoral Traffic Act, commonly abbreviated as SITA, and was later renamed the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act.
accepted.tq: Test the original title directly, a common law-name confusion point.
accepted.sec: Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act 1956 and the Trafficking in Persons Bill

accepted.s: The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 gives effect to which international instrument?
o: The 1948 Universal Declaration of Human Rights alone
The 1992 UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
accepted.x: The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act gives effect to the 1950 UN Convention relating to trafficking and exploitation.
accepted.tq: Match the domestic law with the specific international instrument it implements.
accepted.sec: Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act 1956 and the Trafficking in Persons Bill

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the scope of the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956?
o: It penalises activities such as brothel-keeping, living on the earnings of prostitution, soliciting, detaining persons and clients, but does not criminalise prostitution itself.
It regulates only the registration of protective homes and does not prescribe offences.
It deals exclusively with child trafficking and has no application to brothel-keeping.
It criminalises prostitution itself in every circumstance.
accepted.x: The Act does not criminalise prostitution itself. It penalises specified activities including brothel-keeping, living on prostitution earnings, soliciting, detaining people and clients.
accepted.tq: Separate the underlying activity from the exploitative or facilitating activities made punishable by the law.
accepted.sec: Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act 1956 and the Trafficking in Persons Bill

accepted.s: Under the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, protective homes are run by:
accepted.x: The Act provides for protective homes run by the States.
accepted.tq: Ask which authority operates the protective institution rather than which authority frames the law.
accepted.sec: Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act 1956 and the Trafficking in Persons Bill

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Trafficking in Persons (Prevention, Protection and Rehabilitation) Bill, 2018:
1. It was passed by the Lok Sabha.
2. It lapsed.
3. A draft dealing with the subject followed in 2021.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The 2018 Bill was passed by the Lok Sabha but later lapsed, and a 2021 draft followed it.
accepted.tq: Track the legislative sequence: passage, lapse and subsequent draft.
accepted.sec: Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act 1956 and the Trafficking in Persons Bill

accepted.s: The Victim Protection Plan is intended to provide which of the following through a common protocol?
o: Legal aid, education, skills and livelihood support for rescued victims
accepted.x: The Victim Protection Plan provides a common protocol for legal aid, education, skills and livelihood support to rescued victims.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing the complete rehabilitation-support package.
accepted.sec: Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act 1956 and the Trafficking in Persons Bill

accepted.s: Ujjawala, launched in 2007, covered which combination of activities?
o: Only prosecution and conviction of traffickers
Prevention, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of trafficking victims
accepted.x: Ujjawala covered prevention, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of trafficking victims.
accepted.tq: Recall the four-part programme design instead of reducing the scheme to rescue alone.
accepted.sec: Prevention, rescue and rehabilitation - Ujjawala, AHTUs

accepted.s: Ujjawala is now part of which institutional framework under Mission Shakti?
o: Legal Services Authorities, through Women Helpline 181
accepted.x: Ujjawala is now part of Shakti Sadan under the Samarthya component of Mission Shakti, providing integrated relief homes for trafficked and destitute women.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the rehabilitation framework from emergency response, judicial and legal-aid mechanisms.
accepted.sec: Prevention, rescue and rehabilitation - Ujjawala, AHTUs

accepted.s: Which information system shares real-time alerts on trafficking across States?
accepted.x: Cri-MAC is the Ministry of Home Affairs information technology initiative that shares real-time crime and trafficking alerts across States and supports inter-State coordination.
accepted.tq: Use the function-based distinction between an alert-sharing system, an emergency number and a global report.
accepted.sec: Prevention, rescue and rehabilitation - Ujjawala, AHTUs

accepted.s: The protection under Article 23(1) is available to:
o: Citizens and non-citizens, and operates against the State as well as private persons
Citizens only, unless Parliament extends it to private persons
Citizens only and operates only against the State
Non-citizens only and operates only against private persons
accepted.x: Article 23 is available to both citizens and non-citizens and can be enforced against the State as well as private persons.
accepted.tq: Check both dimensions separately: beneficiaries of the right and entities against whom it operates.
accepted.sec: Constitutional article on traffic in human beings and forced labour

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the scope of Article 23(2)?
o: It applies only to foreign nationals performing public service.
It permits compulsory service only for persons belonging to a particular caste.
It permits compulsory service for public purposes without discrimination on religion, race, caste or class.
It prohibits every form of compulsory service, including service for public purposes.
accepted.x: Article 23(2) permits the State to impose compulsory service for public purposes, but it cannot discriminate on grounds of religion, race, caste or class.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the prohibition in Article 23(1) from the qualified constitutional permission in Article 23(2).
accepted.sec: Constitutional article on traffic in human beings and forced labour

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs of enabling laws is correctly associated with Article 23?
o: ITPA 1956 and Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act 1976
Maternity Benefit Act and RPwD Act alone
Forest Rights Act 2006 and Arms Act 1959
accepted.x: The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 and the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976 are enabling laws associated with Article 23.
accepted.tq: Match the constitutional right with laws directly addressing trafficking and bonded labour.
accepted.sec: Constitutional article on traffic in human beings and forced labour

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 24 prohibits the employment of a child below 14 years in factories, mines or hazardous work.
2. Article 21, understood as the right to life with dignity, forms the basis of mandatory victim rehabilitation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
accepted.x: Both statements are correct. Article 24 protects children below 14 from employment in factories, mines or hazardous work, while Article 21’s life-with-dignity principle supports mandatory victim rehabilitation.
accepted.tq: Test the distinction between the child-labour prohibition in Article 24 and the dignity-based rehabilitation principle under Article 21.
accepted.sec: Constitutional article on traffic in human beings and forced labour

accepted.s:
Under the directions associated with Laxmi v. Union of India, acid may be sold over the counter only when:
1. The purchaser produces a photo identity document.
2. The sale is recorded in a sales register.
3. The purchaser is not below 18 years of age.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Laxmi case directions require photo identification, entry in a sales register and prohibition of sale to anyone below 18 years.
accepted.tq: Verify each safeguard separately before accepting the complete regulatory combination.
accepted.sec: Acid attacks - Laxmi case, sale regulation, compensation

accepted.s: What minimum compensation was directed for victims of acid attacks in Laxmi v. Union of India?
accepted.x: Victims of acid attacks were directed to receive compensation of at least ₹3 lakh.
accepted.tq: Use the statutory minimum rather than confusing it with a higher discretionary amount.
accepted.sec: Acid attacks - Laxmi case, sale regulation, compensation

accepted.s: Apart from compensation, victims of acid attacks are entitled to:
o: Automatic government employment in every case
accepted.x: The directions associated with Laxmi v. Union of India provide free treatment for acid-attack victims in addition to compensation.
accepted.tq: Identify the immediate medical remedy linked with the compensation direction.
accepted.sec: Acid attacks - Laxmi case, sale regulation, compensation

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the legal provisions and punishment relating to acid attacks as given in the relevant framework?
o: Sections 326A and 326B of the IPC, now BNS 124; minimum punishment is 10 years, extendable to life imprisonment.
Sections 302 and 304 of the IPC, now BNS 124; minimum punishment is five years.
Sections 354A and 354B of the IPC, now BNS 181; punishment is fine only.
Sections 124A and 124B of the IPC, now BNS 326; maximum punishment is two years.
accepted.x: Acid-attack offences were covered by Sections 326A and 326B of the IPC and are now identified as BNS 124 in the cited framework. The punishment is a minimum of 10 years, extendable to life imprisonment.
accepted.tq: Keep the section numbers, new code reference and punishment range together to avoid statute-number swaps.
accepted.sec: Acid attacks - Laxmi case, sale regulation, compensation

accepted.s: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 treats acid-attack injuries as:
o: A form of temporary unemployment only
A disability eligible for disability benefits
accepted.x: The RPwD Act, 2016 lists acid-attack injuries as a disability, thereby enabling victims to receive disability benefits.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the disability-law consequence from the criminal-law punishment for the same harm.
accepted.sec: Acid attacks - Laxmi case, sale regulation, compensation
